 Education Experts wonder how federal tax credit scholarships will impact Georgia schools
 The new revenue stream could be a boost or a burden to public schools. Share Gov. Brian Kemp is interviewed after announcing a partnership between the state and the IRS on a new education tax credit in January at the Capitol. (Abbey Cutrer/AJC 2026) By Cassidy Alexander 15 hours ago Public school systems in Georgia are exploring whether they can tap a new well of funding starting in 2027: the first-of-its-kind federal tax credit scholarship program.
 Federal lawmakers created the program as a way for families to pay for things like private school tuition , tutoring, special education services and more. It could be a new revenue steam for cash-strapped public schools — or a drain on their budgets. It’s called the Education Freedom Tax Credit.
 The program is uncapped, meaning every taxpayer in the country could donate if they wished. By 2030, it could rake in $26 billion annually — enough to support millions of students nationwide, according to estimates from the U.S. Treasury and Internal Revenue Service. In time, it could become the largest federal resource accessible for those students, according to some experts.
